title: LATENT-RCT exploratory trial-search candidates (literature only)
status: EXPLORATORY: not part of the analysed set; no specification registered; no data screen run
effect_source: PubMed abstracts retrieved 2026-10-13 via E-utilities efetch (no API key or e-mail); full text not read unless stated

group_definitions.B: feasible with an accepted proxy or a stated adaptation
group_definitions.C: positive (non-null) benchmark for directional tests; tag A or B gives the feasibility class
group_definitions.D: considered but likely infeasible (or ineligible), kept for transparency

candidates.name: CIBIS III
candidates.citation: Willenheimer R, et al. Circulation 2005;112:2426-35
candidates.population: Mild-to-moderate HF (NYHA II-III), LVEF <=35%, age >=65, not on ACEi/ARB/beta-blocker
candidates.intervention: Bisoprolol first (6 months), then bisoprolol + enalapril
candidates.outcome: All-cause death or all-cause hospitalisation
candidates.design: New-user, initial-strategy contrast: first neurohormonal agent in HF patients naive to both classes; no order of the other class in a 30-day grace window (added later in both arms, as in the trial). Time zero = first order of bisoprolol (or cardioselective beta-blocker class) or ACEi.
candidates.ehr: I50.x; echo LVEF <=35%; drug tokens bisoprolol (class: cardioselective beta-blocker) and enalapril (class: ACEi); outcomes all-cause death + any inpatient admission.
candidates.quality: TS 1 (beta-blocker or ACEi class adaptation; a sequence strategy approximated by first-agent choice); CO 1 (ACEi class for enalapril); EL 1 (LVEF from echo, DA if under 50% measured); OU 0 (all-cause death/hospitalisation); FU 0; BM 0.
candidates.why: HF active-comparator trial with all-cause endpoints, complementary to COMET/ELITE II; first-agent choice is plausibly ECG-driven (heart rate, conduction).
candidates.risk: US practice often co-initiates both classes, so the single-agent-first arms may be small.

candidates.name: NORDIL
candidates.citation: Hansson L, et al. Lancet 2000;356:359-65
candidates.population: Hypertension (DBP >=100 mm Hg), age 50-74
candidates.outcome: Fatal/non-fatal stroke, MI, or other CV death
candidates.follow_up: not stated in the abstract (about 4.5 years per secondary sources; unverified)
candidates.design: New-user: diltiazem vs thiazide or beta-blocker as the first antihypertensive. Exclude AF/flutter/SVT (diltiazem is used for rate control). Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: I10; diltiazem token; thiazide and beta-blocker class tokens; exclude I47-I48; outcomes stroke/MI hospitalisation + CV death.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (mixed comparator); OU 1 (CV death); BM 1 (RR); FU 1 if horizon >=48 mo (set 47); TZ.c possible (previously treated patients).
candidates.why: Non-dihydropyridine CCB vs conventional therapy; large null benchmark, and diltiazem initiators are common.
candidates.risk: Confounding by indication for diltiazem (arrhythmia, angina); ECG may help.

candidates.name: ANBP2
candidates.citation: Wing LMH, et al. N Engl J Med 2003;348:583-92
candidates.population: Hypertension, age 65-84, Australian family practice
candidates.outcome: First cardiovascular event or death from any cause
candidates.design: New-user active comparator: first antihypertensive order (ACEi vs thiazide), none in the prior 365 days. Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: I10-I15; ACEi class and thiazide-class tokens; outcomes all-cause death + first CV-coded inpatient stay (I20-I25, I50, I60-I66, I70-I74).
candidates.quality: TS 1, CO 1 (class adaptations); OU 1 (the broad 'any CV event' composite is approximated by CV hospitalisations; outpatient events are missed); FU 0 if horizon <48 mo (use 47); TZ.c to be checked (proportion previously treated); BM 0.
candidates.why: Pragmatic primary-care trial of first-line class with a tight near-null CI; ACEi vs thiazide is not in the analysed set (ALLHAT's lisinopril arm was never built).
candidates.risk: The thiazide arm overlaps the ALLHAT and INSIGHT cohorts; run the record-overlap check.

candidates.name: SURPASS-CVOT
candidates.citation: Nicholls SJ, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:2409-20
candidates.population: T2D with established ASCVD, BMI >=25
candidates.outcome: CV death, MI or stroke

effect.text: HR 0.92 (95.3% CI 0.83-1.01); P=0.003 noninferiority, P=0.09 superiority

candidates.design: New-user active comparator in T2D + ASCVD: tirzepatide (approved May 2022) vs dulaglutide initiators, with no GLP-1RA in the prior 365 days. Index window 2022-06 to 2024. Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: E11 + ASCVD codes; tokens tirzepatide (exclude obesity-only Zepbound without T2D), dulaglutide; 3-point MACE.
candidates.quality: FU 1 (FU.b: the available horizon of at most ~2.5 y is much shorter than the trial's); OU 1 (CV death); BM 0 (noninferiority HR, 95.3% CI); DA risk (event count in a short window).
candidates.why: The only large incretin head-to-head CVOT with a hard endpoint; true active comparator; very high use late in the window.

candidates.name: PRoFESS
candidates.citation: Sacco RL, et al. N Engl J Med 2008;359:1238-51
candidates.population: Recent non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke (<90 days)
candidates.outcome: Recurrent stroke
candidates.design: New-user active comparator after ischaemic stroke: first order of the aspirin/dipyridamole combination product vs clopidogrel within 90 days of the index stroke. Exclude AF and anticoagulant users. Time zero = first order (inpatient or discharge).
candidates.ehr: I63; combination token aspirin-dipyridamole (Aggrenox), clopidogrel; exclude I48 and OAC; outcome stroke hospitalisation (I60-I64) after the index stay.
candidates.quality: TS 0, CO 0; TZ 0 (both arms start at the same point; inpatient orders are visible); OU 0-1 (recurrent vs index stroke separated by excluding the index stay); ES risk (higher discontinuation of ASA-ERDP); DA risk (ASA-ERDP use declined).
candidates.why: Large active-comparator secondary-stroke trial; adds the cerebrovascular domain, which the pool lacks.

candidates.name: TASTE
candidates.citation: Frobert O, et al. N Engl J Med 2013;369:1587-97
candidates.population: STEMI undergoing primary PCI (registry-based, Scandinavia)
candidates.outcome: All-cause death at 30 days
candidates.design: Procedure add-on within a common procedure (as LAAOS III): primary PCI for STEMI with vs without a same-session aspiration thrombectomy code. Time zero = PCI date.
candidates.ehr: I21.0-I21.3; PCI CPT 92941 / ICD-10-PCS 027-; thrombectomy CPT 92973 / ICD-10-PCS 02C-; outcome all-cause death (death records, including in-hospital deaths).
candidates.quality: TZ 0 (common time zero); TS 0; CO 0; OU 0 (all-cause death); FU 0; DA risk (thrombectomy use fell after 2015).
candidates.why: Registry-embedded RCT (the closest RCT design to EHR emulation) with an all-cause-death endpoint; STEMI ECG physiology is central to both thrombus burden and prognosis.
candidates.risk: Strong confounding by thrombus burden (angiographic, not coded). TOTAL is an alternative benchmark (Group D, near-duplicate).

candidates.name: CTOPP
candidates.citation: Connolly SJ, et al. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1385-91
candidates.population: First pacemaker for symptomatic bradycardia, no chronic AF
candidates.outcome: Stroke or CV death
candidates.design: Device vs device at first implant: dual-chamber vs single-chamber ventricular pacemaker (leadless VVI included) in patients without AF. Time zero = implant date.
candidates.ehr: Bradycardia/AV block/SND codes (I44.1-I44.2, I49.5, R00.1); CPT 33208 vs 33207 (and leadless 33274); exclude I48; outcome stroke hospitalisation + CV death.
candidates.quality: EL 1 (exclude AF); TS 0; CO 0; OU 1 (CV death); BM 1 (RRR, not HR); confounding by frailty (single-chamber devices go to frail patients), where ECG conduction features are directly relevant.
candidates.why: Device-vs-device contrast in which the ECG is the indication; UKPACE and MOST are alternative benchmarks (Group D).

candidates.name: EVAR trial 1
candidates.citation: EVAR trial investigators (Greenhalgh RM, et al.). N Engl J Med 2010;362:1863-71; 4-year report Lancet 2005;365:2179-86
candidates.population: AAA >=5.5 cm, age >=60, fit for open repair
candidates.outcome: All-cause death (long term); aneurysm-related death

effect.text: All-cause death adjusted HR 1.03 (0.86-1.23); 30-day operative mortality adjusted OR 0.39 (0.18-0.87); 4-year all-cause death HR 0.90 (0.69-1.18) (Lancet 2005, PMID 15978925)

candidates.design: Procedure vs procedure: first elective repair of non-ruptured AAA, EVAR vs open. Time zero = repair date. A 4-year all-cause-death horizon matches the 2005 report.
candidates.ehr: I71.4; EVAR CPT 34701-34708 / ICD-10-PCS 04V03DZ etc.; open CPT 35081/35102 / 04R0-, 04V00-; outcome all-cause death.
candidates.quality: EL 1-2 ('fit for open repair' cannot be identified, so EVAR includes unfit patients); TS 0, CO 0, OU 0; BM 1 for the 2010 adjusted HR (use the 2005 4-year HR); FU 0 with a 48-month horizon.
candidates.why: Procedure-vs-procedure trial with an all-cause-death endpoint and strong confounding by frailty, a demanding test of ECG-augmented balance.

candidates.name: SCOT
candidates.citation: MacDonald TM, et al. Eur Heart J 2017;38:1843-50
candidates.population: Age >=60, OA/RA on chronic prescribed non-selective NSAID, no CVD
candidates.outcome: Hospitalisation for non-fatal MI/ACS, non-fatal stroke, or CV death
candidates.design: Sequential switch (switch_seq, as FRAIL-AF): established prescribed-nsNSAID users who switch to celecoxib vs continuers sampled within +/-30 days. Time zero = switch date.
candidates.ehr: M05-M06, M15-M19; tokens diclofenac, ibuprofen, naproxen, meloxicam, etc. (prescribed); celecoxib; exclude CVD; outcome MI/stroke hospitalisation + CV death.
candidates.quality: CO 0 (continuation); TS 0; OU 1 (CV death); ES 0 using the ITT benchmark (the trial's primary was on-treatment); DA risk (low event rate, ~1.1/100 PY).
candidates.why: Tests the switch design in a second drug class; complements PRECISION (new users) without reusing its cohort.

candidates.name: INVESTED
candidates.citation: Vardeny O, et al. JAMA 2021;325:39-49
candidates.population: Recent MI or HF hospitalisation plus >=1 risk factor
candidates.outcome: All-cause death or cardiopulmonary hospitalisation (per season)
candidates.design: Season-specific new-user: patients with an MI or HF hospitalisation in the prior 12 months vaccinated Sep-Jan; arm by vaccine formulation. Time zero = vaccination date; follow-up to the season end. First season only.
candidates.ehr: CVX/CPT vaccine codes (high-dose CVX 135/197, CPT 90662; standard-dose quadrivalent CVX 150/158/161/171); I21/I50 hospitalisation; outcome death or principal-diagnosis cardiopulmonary admission.
candidates.quality: TS 0 (formulation coded); EL 1 (risk-factor enrichment; high-dose licensed >=65, so restrict to >=65); OU 1 (cardiopulmonary definition); vaccination capture outside the system (pharmacies) is incomplete.
candidates.why: EHR-native exposure with an active comparator, all-cause outcomes and a high-risk CV population; a very common exposure.

candidates.name: SWEDEPAD 1
candidates.citation: Falkenberg M, et al. Lancet 2025;406:1103-14
candidates.population: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (Rutherford 4-6) undergoing infrainguinal endovascular treatment
candidates.outcome: Ipsilateral major (above-ankle) amputation
candidates.design: Device contrast within a common procedure: CLTI endovascular revascularisation with vs without a drug-coated device. Time zero = procedure date.
candidates.ehr: I70.22-I70.26 / I70.23x-I70.26x; endovascular CPT 37224-37235; drug-coated device from ICD-10-PCS device qualifiers (drug-coated balloon / drug-eluting intraluminal device) or HCPCS C2623; outcome amputation CPT 27590-27598, 27880-27889 / ICD-10-PCS 0Y6-.
candidates.quality: TS 1 (device identification depends on PCS qualifiers or HCPCS; laterality is needed for 'ipsilateral'); OU 1 (laterality); CO 0; EL 0; calendar confounding (paclitaxel mortality signal 2018-2019).
candidates.why: Registry-based RCT with a procedure-coded endpoint; a device-safety question that matters in the current window.
candidates.risk: Index dates are shared with BEST-CLI and VOYAGER PAD cohorts; check overlap.

candidates.name: STICH (hypothesis 1)
candidates.citation: Velazquez EJ, et al. N Engl J Med 2011;364:1607-16; extended (STICHES) N Engl J Med 2016;374:1511-20 (PMID 27040723)
candidates.population: CAD amenable to CABG with LVEF <=35%
candidates.outcome: All-cause death
candidates.design: Strategy at a common decision point: diagnostic angiography in ischaemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF <=35%), CABG within a 30-60 day grace period vs no CABG. Needs clone-censor-weighting, which is not yet in the pipeline.
candidates.ehr: Cath CPT 93454-93461; CABG CPT 33510-33536; echo LVEF; outcome all-cause death.
candidates.quality: TZ.d (grace period/immortal time must be handled); EL 1 ('amenable to CABG'); CO 1 (non-surgical arm includes surgical non-candidates); FU 1 (>=48 mo); ES (crossover).
candidates.why: Landmark HFrEF revascularisation trial with an all-cause-death endpoint; LV physiology is central.

candidates.name: IRONMAN
candidates.citation: Kalra PR, et al. Lancet 2022;400:2199-209
candidates.population: HF with LVEF <=45% and iron deficiency (TSAT <20% or ferritin <100)
candidates.outcome: Recurrent HF hospitalisation and CV death
candidates.design: Initiation vs non-initiation after a qualifying iron panel: HF patient with qualifying labs; IV iron within a 30-day grace period vs none. Time zero = lab date; clone-censor-weight.
candidates.ehr: I50; ferritin/TSAT labs; IV iron HCPCS J1437/J1439/J1756/J2916 or infusion orders; outcome HF hospitalisation + CV death.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (usual-care comparator, matching the open-label trial); TZ.d (grace period); OU 1 (first-event analysis changes the estimand from recurrent events); BM 1 (rate ratio); EL 0 (lab-defined).
candidates.why: Eligibility is defined by labs, which is an EHR strength; AFFIRM-AHF and HEART-FID are placebo-controlled alternative benchmarks.

candidates.name: EXSCEL
candidates.citation: Holman RR, et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:1228-39
candidates.population: T2D with or without CVD (73% with CVD)
candidates.outcome: CV death, non-fatal MI or non-fatal stroke
candidates.design: RCT-DUPLICATE placebo proxy: exenatide ER vs DPP-4i new users (as LEADER). Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: E11; tokens exenatide (weekly formulation) vs DPP-4i; 3-point MACE.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (proxy); OU 1 (CV death); FU 0 (38 mo); DA risk (exenatide ER use is modest; the LEADER liraglutide arm had 453 with an ECG).
candidates.why: Completes the GLP-1RA CVOT family under the accepted proxy; benchmark at the null boundary.

candidates.name: COURAGE
candidates.citation: Boden WE, et al. N Engl J Med 2007;356:1503-16
candidates.population: Stable CAD with objective ischaemia and >=70% stenosis
candidates.outcome: All-cause death or non-fatal MI
candidates.design: Decision point = elective diagnostic angiography with obstructive CAD in stable patients (no ACS in 30 days). PCI within a 30-day grace period vs no revascularisation (CABG excluded). Clone-censor-weight.
candidates.ehr: Cath CPT 93454-93461; I25.x without I20.0/I21-I24 in 30 days; PCI CPT 92928-92944; outcome death + MI hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: TZ.d (grace period); EL 1 (ischaemia and anatomy not coded); CO 1; ES (33% crossover to PCI in the trial); FU 1 if horizon >=48 (use a 36-mo landmark).
candidates.why: Landmark stable-CAD strategy trial with a null benchmark; ISCHEMIA is the alternative (Group D).

candidates.name: VALIDATE-SWEDEHEART
candidates.citation: Erlinge D, et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:1132-42
candidates.population: STEMI or NSTEMI undergoing PCI on a potent P2Y12 inhibitor, no planned GPI
candidates.outcome: Death, MI or major bleeding at 180 days
candidates.design: In-hospital procedural anticoagulant contrast at PCI for MI: bivalirudin vs UFH-only. Time zero = PCI date.
candidates.ehr: I21; PCI codes; bivalirudin/heparin administrations (cath-lab MAR); outcome all-cause death + post-discharge MI/major-bleeding hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: OU 1-2 (index-stay MI/bleeding excluded by the current rule); TS/SI risk (cath-lab drugs may be documented outside order tables); CO 0.
candidates.why: Registry-based RCT with a null benchmark; tests in-hospital drug exposure. BRIGHT-4, HEAT-PPCI, EUROMAX, HORIZONS-AMI and MATRIX are alternatives (Group D).

candidates.name: EMPACT-MI
candidates.citation: Butler J, et al. N Engl J Med 2024;390:1455-66
candidates.population: Acute MI with new LVEF <45% and/or congestion, within 14 days
candidates.outcome: First HF hospitalisation or all-cause death
candidates.design: Placebo proxy restricted to T2D: SGLT2i vs DPP-4i initiation within 14 days of the MI admission (inpatient orders visible). Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: I21; LVEF from echo; E11; SGLT2i/DPP-4i tokens; outcome HF hospitalisation + all-cause death.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (DPP-4i proxy); EL 2 (T2D restriction; only a minority of trial patients had diabetes); TZ 0 (in-hospital orders visible, as for the PLATO exemption); OU 0.
candidates.why: Post-MI SGLT2i null benchmark; complements PARADISE-MI.

candidates.name: TACSI
candidates.citation: Jeppsson A, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:2313-23
candidates.population: ACS treated with isolated CABG
candidates.outcome: Death, MI, stroke or repeat revascularisation at 1 year

effect.text: HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.72-1.56); net adverse clinical events HR 1.45

candidates.design: Common decision point = CABG for ACS: ticagrelor initiation within 14 days of surgery (discharge) vs no P2Y12 inhibitor (aspirin background assumed). Time zero = CABG date + grace period.
candidates.ehr: I21-I24 index; CABG CPT 33510-33536; ticagrelor token; outcomes death, MI/stroke hospitalisation, repeat revascularisation procedures.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (non-initiator comparator, matching the open-label trial; aspirin not identifiable); TZ.d (grace period); OU 1 (needs repeat-revascularisation procedure outcome); FU 0.
candidates.why: Recent registry-based pragmatic RCT anchored at a common decision point.

candidates.name: EINSTEIN-DVT
candidates.citation: EINSTEIN Investigators (Bauersachs R, et al.). N Engl J Med 2010;363:2499-510
candidates.population: Acute symptomatic proximal DVT without PE
candidates.outcome: Recurrent VTE
candidates.design: New-user active comparator after acute DVT (as AMPLIFY): rivaroxaban vs warfarin (with parenteral lead-in). Exclude PE. Time zero = first anticoagulant order.
candidates.ehr: I82.4x acute (no I26); rivaroxaban, warfarin, enoxaparin; outcome recurrent VTE as a new inpatient stay with a VTE code.
candidates.quality: OU 2 (inpatient-only recurrent VTE, as AMPLIFY); TS 0, CO 0 (VKA); FU 0; BM 0.
candidates.why: RCT-DUPLICATE trial (legacy v1 config exists) that is missing from the current pool; uses a common DOAC.
candidates.risk: Warfarin arm overlaps AMPLIFY's comparator; check the record share.

candidates.name: EINSTEIN-PE
candidates.citation: EINSTEIN-PE Investigators (Buller HR, et al.). N Engl J Med 2012;366:1287-97
candidates.population: Acute symptomatic PE with or without DVT
candidates.outcome: Recurrent VTE
candidates.design: As EINSTEIN-DVT, in PE (I26), which gives a cohort disjoint from EINSTEIN-DVT.
candidates.ehr: I26.x; rivaroxaban, warfarin, enoxaparin; recurrent VTE hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: OU 2 (as AMPLIFY); TS 0; CO 0; FU 0.
candidates.why: RCT-DUPLICATE trial missing from the current pool; together with EINSTEIN-DVT it gives a DVT/PE pair.

candidates.name: RE-MEDY (active-control study)
candidates.citation: Schulman S, et al. N Engl J Med 2013;368:709-18
candidates.population: VTE treated for 3-12 months, at elevated recurrence risk
candidates.outcome: Recurrent or fatal VTE
candidates.design: Sequential switch (switch_seq): established warfarin users >=3 months after VTE who switch to dabigatran vs continuers sampled within +/-30 days.
candidates.ehr: VTE codes; warfarin then dabigatran orders; recurrent VTE hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: OU 2; EL 1; DA risk; CO 0.
candidates.why: Switch design in VTE, parallel to FRAIL-AF in AF.

candidates.name: RE-COVER II
candidates.citation: Schulman S, et al. Circulation 2014;129:764-72
candidates.population: Acute VTE after 5-11 days of parenteral anticoagulation
candidates.outcome: Recurrent symptomatic VTE or related death at 6 months
candidates.design: Sequential: first oral anticoagulant after >=5 days of parenteral heparin/LMWH, dabigatran vs warfarin. Time zero = first oral order.
candidates.ehr: I26/I82; heparin/enoxaparin; dabigatran, warfarin; recurrent VTE hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: OU 2; DA risk (low dabigatran use for VTE); CO 0.
candidates.why: RCT-DUPLICATE trial missing from the current pool; RE-COVER is its twin (Group D, near-duplicate).

candidates.name: CARAVAGGIO
candidates.citation: Agnelli G, et al. N Engl J Med 2020;382:1599-607
candidates.population: Cancer-associated acute VTE
candidates.outcome: Recurrent VTE at 6 months
candidates.design: New-user: apixaban vs LMWH (enoxaparin/dalteparin class adaptation) in active cancer with acute VTE. Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: C00-C96 with recent oncology treatment; I26/I82; apixaban; enoxaparin/dalteparin; recurrent VTE hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (LMWH class); OU 2; EL 1 (active cancer from codes and chemotherapy orders); FU 0.
candidates.why: Guideline-defining cancer-VTE trial, DOAC vs LMWH.

candidates.name: CREST
candidates.citation: Brott TG, et al. N Engl J Med 2010;363:11-23
candidates.population: Symptomatic or asymptomatic carotid stenosis
candidates.outcome: Periprocedural stroke, MI or death, or ipsilateral stroke within 4 years
candidates.design: Procedure vs procedure: first carotid revascularisation, CAS (including TCAR) vs CEA. Time zero = procedure date.
candidates.ehr: I65.2x (+ I63/G45 history for 'symptomatic'); CAS CPT 37215/37216 / ICD-10-PCS 037K3-/037L3-; CEA CPT 35301 / 03CK0ZZ, 03CL0ZZ.
candidates.quality: Adaptation needed: OU 2 under the current rule, because periprocedural events happen in the index stay; count in-stay post-procedure events (POA = N) or accept OU 2. EL 1 (stenosis degree not coded); TS 0, CO 0.
candidates.why: High-impact US carotid trial (procedure vs procedure); ICSS, ACST-2, ACT-1 and SPACE give stratum-specific alternative benchmarks.

candidates.name: RAFT
candidates.citation: Tang ASL, et al. N Engl J Med 2010;363:2385-95
candidates.population: NYHA II-III HF, LVEF <=30%, QRS >=120 ms (or paced >=200 ms)
candidates.outcome: All-cause death or HF hospitalisation
candidates.design: Device vs device at first implant: CRT-D vs ICD-only in HFrEF with a wide QRS. Time zero = implant date. QRS duration/morphology from the raw pre-implant ECG.
candidates.ehr: I50; LVEF <=30%; ECG QRS >=120 ms; CPT 33249 with vs without 33225 (LV lead) / ICD-10-PCS generator device values; outcome death + HF hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: EL 0-1 (QRS and LVEF measured); TS 0, CO 0; OU 0-1 (HF hospitalisation coding position); FU 0; DA (count of CRT-D vs ICD-only implants to be checked).
candidates.why: Positive device benchmark in which the ECG defines eligibility and modifies the effect (QRS/LBBB), a direct test of whether ECG embeddings carry treatment-relevant physiology. MADIT-CRT is an alternative benchmark (Group D, near-duplicate).

candidates.name: DAPA-CKD
candidates.citation: Heerspink HJL, et al. N Engl J Med 2020;383:1436-46
candidates.population: CKD (eGFR 25-75, UACR 200-5000), with or without T2D (two-thirds with T2D)
candidates.outcome: Sustained eGFR decline >=50%, ESKD, or renal or CV death
candidates.design: Placebo proxy in the T2D stratum: SGLT2i vs DPP-4i new users with qualifying eGFR/UACR labs. Lab-based endpoint: confirmed (>=28 d) eGFR decline >=50%, dialysis/transplant codes, renal or CV death.
candidates.ehr: eGFR/UACR labs; E11; SGLT2i/DPP-4i tokens; N18.6, Z99.2, dialysis CPT 90935-90999; outcome per above.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (proxy); EL 1 (T2D restriction; UACR measured in a subset, so DA); OU 1 (lab-based composite, renal death by cause); FU 0.
candidates.why: Very strong positive benchmark with lab-defined population and endpoint (an EHR strength); emulated in RCT-DUPLICATE; legacy v1 config exists.

candidates.name: SOUL
candidates.citation: McGuire DK, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:2001-12
candidates.population: T2D, age >=50, with ASCVD and/or CKD
candidates.outcome: CV death, MI or stroke
candidates.design: Placebo proxy: oral semaglutide (tablet formulation; marketed Sep 2019+) vs DPP-4i new users. Time zero = first order.
candidates.ehr: E11 + ASCVD/CKD; semaglutide TABLET formulation token (must be separable from injectable); DPP-4i; 3-point MACE.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (proxy); TS 1 (formulation must be distinguishable, or the cohort merges with SUSTAIN-6); FU 1 (horizon >=48 mo unless truncated); DA risk.
candidates.why: Recent positive proxy CVOT; PIONEER 6 is an alternative benchmark (Group D, near-duplicate).

candidates.name: TACTICS-TIMI 18
candidates.citation: Cannon CP, et al. N Engl J Med 2001;344:1879-87
candidates.population: UA/NSTEMI with ST/T changes, raised markers or CAD history
candidates.outcome: Death, non-fatal MI or ACS rehospitalisation at 6 months
candidates.design: Decision point = NSTE-ACS admission: coronary angiography within 48 h vs not within 48 h (clone-censor). ST/T changes can be read from the admission ECG.
candidates.ehr: I21.4/I24.9/I20.0; angiography CPT 93454-93461 timing; outcome death, MI and ACS readmissions.
candidates.quality: TZ.d (grace period); CO 1; ES (about half of conservative-arm patients had angiography in hospital); BM 1 (OR); era differs (1997-2000 tirofiban use); FU 0.
candidates.why: Positive strategy benchmark with ECG-defined eligibility. FRISC II, RITA-3, ICTUS and SENIOR-RITA are alternatives (Group D).

candidates.name: FREEDOM
candidates.citation: Farkouh ME, et al. N Engl J Med 2012;367:2375-84
candidates.population: Diabetes with multivessel CAD (83% three-vessel), no left main
candidates.outcome: All-cause death, non-fatal MI or non-fatal stroke

effect.text: 5-year rate 26.6% PCI vs 18.7% CABG, P=0.005 (CABG better); no HR reported in the abstract

candidates.design: Procedure vs procedure in diabetes: multivessel PCI (>=2 vessels by CPT add-on codes) vs CABG with >=2 grafts. Time zero = revascularisation date.
candidates.ehr: E10/E11; PCI CPT 92928 + 92929/92934/92938/92944 (or C9600-C9608); CABG CPT 33510-33536 (graft counts); outcome death + MI/stroke hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: EL 1-2 (anatomy approximated by vessel/graft counts; left main not excluded); OU 1 (periprocedural index-stay MI excluded); BM 1 (rates/P only in the abstract; extract an HR from the full text); FU 1 if horizon >=48.
candidates.why: Landmark positive procedural benchmark (CABG superior) with heavy confounding by anatomy and frailty. SYNTAX, EXCEL, NOBLE and FAME 3 are alternatives (Group D).

candidates.name: COMPASS
candidates.citation: Eikelboom JW, et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:1319-30
candidates.population: Stable CAD or PAD
candidates.outcome: CV death, stroke or MI
candidates.design: Sequential add-on vs continuation in CAD/PAD without an anticoagulation indication: rivaroxaban 2.5 mg initiation vs established antiplatelet-only users sampled within +/-30 days.
candidates.ehr: I25/I70.2; rivaroxaban 2.5 mg STRENGTH (needs dose-level tokens); exclude I48, I26, I82; 3-point MACE.
candidates.quality: TS 1-2 (strength identification); CO 2 (placebo-controlled; non-initiator comparator); OU 1 (CV death); DA risk (vascular-dose uptake); FU 0.
candidates.why: Very large positive benchmark. VOYAGER PAD gives the same drug a cleaner time zero.

candidates.name: POINT
candidates.citation: Johnston SC, et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:215-25
candidates.population: Minor ischaemic stroke (NIHSS <=3) or high-risk TIA, within 12 h
candidates.outcome: Ischaemic stroke, MI or ischaemic vascular death at 90 days
candidates.design: ED/admission decision point: clopidogrel order within 24 h vs none (aspirin ordered in both; inpatient orders visible). Time zero = presentation.
candidates.ehr: I63/G45 with an NIHSS flowsheet value if available; clopidogrel/aspirin inpatient orders; outcome ischaemic stroke/MI hospitalisation + vascular death.
candidates.quality: OU 2 risk (most recurrences fall in the first days, inside the index stay; adaptation: count in-stay events after day 1 with POA = N); EL 1 (NIHSS/ABCD2); CO 2 (placebo add-on; non-initiator); FU 0.
candidates.why: Positive, guideline-defining stroke trial; CHANCE is an alternative (Group D).

candidates.name: TALOS-AMI
candidates.citation: Kim CJ, et al. Lancet 2021;398:1305-16
candidates.population: AMI after PCI, event-free on ticagrelor + aspirin for 1 month (Korea)
candidates.outcome: CV death, MI, stroke or BARC 2/3/5 bleeding at 12 months
candidates.design: Sequential switch (switch_seq): about 1 month after MI-PCI, ticagrelor users who switch to clopidogrel vs continuers sampled within +/-30 days.
candidates.ehr: I21 + PCI; ticagrelor, then clopidogrel orders; outcomes CV death, MI/stroke hospitalisation, bleeding hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: OU 2 (BARC 2 bleeding, the dominant component, is not ascertainable, as for FRAIL-AF); EL 1 (East Asian population; event-free at 1 month); CO 0; FU 0.
candidates.why: Positive switch-design benchmark in ACS, parallel to FRAIL-AF in AF.

candidates.name: BETAMI-DANBLOCK
candidates.citation: Munkhaugen J, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:1901-11
candidates.population: MI within 14 days with LVEF >=40% (Norway/Denmark)
candidates.outcome: All-cause death, MI, unplanned revascularisation, ischaemic stroke, HF or malignant ventricular arrhythmia
candidates.design: MI admission with LVEF >=40%: beta-blocker initiated in hospital or within 14 days vs not (grace period; prior beta-blocker users excluded). Time zero = MI admission.
candidates.ehr: I21; echo LVEF >=40%; beta-blocker tokens (inpatient + discharge); outcomes death, MI/stroke/HF hospitalisations, revascularisation procedures, I47.2/I49.0 events.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (no-treatment comparator, matching the open-label trial); TZ 0 (in-hospital orders visible); TZ.d (grace period); OU 1 (composite with revascularisation and arrhythmia); FU 0 (42 mo); strong confounding (non-use is selective).
candidates.why: Contemporary, guideline-changing, ECG-relevant (heart rate, arrhythmia). REDUCE-AMI (0.96) and REBOOT (1.04) are same-question benchmarks on an overlapping cohort (Group D), a natural test of benchmark heterogeneity.

candidates.name: IMPROVE-IT
candidates.citation: Cannon CP, et al. N Engl J Med 2015;372:2387-97
candidates.population: ACS within 10 days, LDL 50-125 mg/dL
candidates.outcome: CV death, MI, UA hospitalisation, coronary revascularisation >=30 days, or stroke
candidates.design: Decision point = ACS admission: statin + ezetimibe initiation within 10 days vs statin alone (non-initiator of ezetimibe).
candidates.ehr: I21-I24 + LDL lab; statin and ezetimibe tokens; outcome needs coronary revascularisation procedures >=30 days plus UA hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (placebo add-on; non-initiator comparator); OU 1-2 (revascularisation component needs a procedure-based outcome; LODESTAR lacked it); FU 1 (>=48 mo unless truncated); small effect, so low directional power.
candidates.why: Canonical lipid add-on benchmark; its small positive effect tests the resolution of the agreement metrics.

candidates.name: REDUCE-IT
candidates.citation: Bhatt DL, et al. N Engl J Med 2019;380:11-22
candidates.population: Established CVD or diabetes + risk factors, on statin, triglycerides 135-499 mg/dL
candidates.outcome: CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularisation or UA
candidates.design: Stated active-comparator proxy (not an RCT-DUPLICATE convention): icosapent ethyl vs omega-3-acid ethyl esters (EPA+DHA) new users among statin users with a qualifying TG lab. The proxy rests on null hard-outcome trials of EPA+DHA products (STRENGTH, VITAL, ASCEND).
candidates.ehr: TG lab; statin tokens; icosapent ethyl vs omega-3-acid ethyl esters (prescription); outcome MACE + revascularisation procedures + UA hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: CO 2 (proxy; mineral-oil placebo may have inflated the benchmark); OU 1 (revascularisation and UA components); FU 1 if horizon >=48; EL 0.
candidates.why: Strong positive benchmark with lab-defined eligibility; it would explicitly test a new, prespecified proxy. JELIS and RESPECT-EPA are alternatives (Group D).

candidates.name: DapaTAVI
candidates.citation: Raposeiras-Roubin S, et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:1396-405
candidates.population: Severe AS undergoing TAVI with HF history, LVEF <=40%, diabetes or CKD; not on SGLT2i
candidates.outcome: All-cause death or worsening HF (hospitalisation or urgent visit) at 1 year
candidates.design: Common decision point = TAVR: SGLT2i initiation within 14-30 days of TAVR vs none (grace period, clone-censor). Excludes prior SGLT2i users.
candidates.ehr: TAVR CPT 33361-33366 / ICD-10-PCS 02RF3-; SGLT2i tokens; I50/LVEF/E11/N18; outcome death + HF hospitalisation.
candidates.quality: CO 1 (no-treatment comparator, matching the open-label trial); TZ.d (grace period); OU 1 (urgent outpatient HF visits missed); FU 0.
candidates.why: Recent positive trial anchored at a procedure.
candidates.risk: TAVR index dates overlap the previously analysed PARTNER cohort; the 80% rule may need an interpretation (different contrast, same records).

candidates.name: VOYAGER PAD
candidates.citation: Bonaca MP, et al. N Engl J Med 2020;382:1994-2004
candidates.population: Symptomatic PAD after lower-extremity revascularisation (within 10 days)
candidates.outcome: Acute limb ischaemia, major vascular amputation, MI, ischaemic stroke or CV death
candidates.design: Common decision point = lower-extremity revascularisation: rivaroxaban 2.5 mg initiation within 10 days vs none. Time zero = procedure date + grace period.
candidates.ehr: I70.2x; revascularisation CPT 37224-37235/35556-35671; rivaroxaban 2.5 mg strength; outcomes ALI (I74.3/I74.4), amputation procedures, MI/stroke, CV death.
candidates.quality: TS 1-2 (strength); CO 2 (placebo; non-initiator comparator); TZ.d (10-day grace period); OU 1 (CV death; ALI coding); FU 0.
candidates.why: Positive benchmark anchored at a procedure; complements BEST-CLI/SWEDEPAD 1 in a vascular area that is new to the project.

candidates.name: BEST-CLI (cohort 1)
candidates.citation: Farber A, et al. N Engl J Med 2022;387:2305-16
candidates.population: CLTI eligible for either revascularisation with an adequate great saphenous vein
candidates.outcome: Major adverse limb event (above-ankle amputation or major reintervention) or death
candidates.design: Procedure vs procedure: first revascularisation for CLTI, open bypass vs endovascular. Time zero = procedure date.
candidates.ehr: I70.22-I70.26; bypass CPT 35556-35671 / ICD-10-PCS 041-; endovascular CPT 37224-37235; outcome amputation and reintervention procedures + all-cause death.
candidates.quality: EL 1 (vein adequacy not identifiable, so cohorts 1 and 2 mix); TS 0; CO 0; OU 0-1 (reintervention definition); FU 0.
candidates.why: Strongly positive procedure-vs-procedure benchmark with procedure-coded endpoints; heavy confounding by frailty.
candidates.risk: Shares endovascular index dates with SWEDEPAD 1 and VOYAGER PAD; select or check overlap.
